Case Study: The Spreading Oil Slick

Read the passage carefully, then answer the 5 MCQs in the test below.

A tanker develops a small leak just outside a harbour, and a thin film of oil begins to spread across the calm sea as a growing circle. Marine officers on the pier observe that the radius of the circular slick increases at a steady 2 metres every second. Because the area covered is A=π r², the officers can predict how quickly the polluted region expands and how fast its circular boundary lengthens as clean-up boats are dispatched. When the radius reaches 25 metres they record the instantaneous rate at which the area is growing. Some time later a shift in the current makes the enclosed area itself increase at a constant 80π square metres per second; with the radius then 10 metres, they work backwards to find how fast the radius is moving outward at that instant.
